name: TeamPCP
description: TeamPCP is a financially motivated supply chain threat actor that pivoted from ransomware/cryptomining to focused software supply chain compromise in early 2026. Best known for the March 2026 cascading campaign compromising Trivy, KICS, LiteLLM, and Telnyx Python SDK, and the May 2026 Mini Shai-Hulud campaign targeting TanStack, Mistral AI, UiPath, and OpenSearch via CI cache poisoning. Operates as an access broker, with stolen credentials monetized by ransomware groups including Vect.

detection_opportunities: Anomalous npm publish events from CI/CD service accounts
Unexpected GitHub repository creation by developer accounts
Cloud API calls (AWS/GCP/Azure) originating from CI pipeline infrastructure
GitHub Actions workflow modifications in pull requests from forks
New OIDC token issuance outside normal deployment windows
Secrets accessed in CI environment outside expected job context
response_playbook: Audit recent npm/PyPI publish events from CI/CD service accounts for unauthorized package versions.
Review GitHub Actions workflow files for modifications introduced via fork pull requests (cache-poisoning vector).
Rotate any credentials that transited CI pipelines, especially OIDC trusted-publisher tokens.
Inventory dependencies for known-compromised packages (Shai-Hulud/Mini variant, Trivy-related) and pin or replace them.
Check for new, unexpected GitHub repositories created by developer or CI service accounts.
Scan build environments for steganographic payloads (WAV files) and .pth-based auto-execution artifacts.
